args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback: service healthy, error rate 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging prior to the production deploy. Follow-up: root-cause the v2.3.1 regression before re-deploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west. 18% of requests were failing.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it, and the failure rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It also notes that the v2.3.1 release candidate was already unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. Someone should find out why it shipped anyway and fix v2.3.1 before it's deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
